## Existing cycle and correction

Original runOwned response-loss/unknown path waits on original progress.awaitCompletion with the exact lease/genuine proof. Only original confirmCompletion after consumed/saved source receipt/proofId/current checks resolves that deferred. Original execution.stop awaits operation.done including that callback/finally. Parent cleared interval before awaiting execution.stop and placed recovery only after it; a callback entering pendingCompletion before or during stop could not reach normal recovery.

runner keeps the existing setInterval(wake,2000) alive while original execution.stop is pending. stopped=true disables admission; wake calls sweepMachine(c,false) while stopping, with the same serialized active Promise. Immediately after original execution.stop is invoked, wake also requests recovery, while the unchanged interval covers late pendingCompletion after that initial sweep. Original sweepMachine proof verification/finishInput/current/confirmCompletion/claim logic is not edited. No direct deferred resolve/new proof/ACK/native events or boolean completion substitution. This is normal same-proof recovery, not timeout success.

Stop is a cached Promise. It sets stopped synchronously, awaits any already-issued active sweep, cancels existing inputs, captures/invokes original execution.stop once, invokes recovery wake and awaits the captured original Promise. On original settlement, finally sets finished=true, clears the one existing timer and awaits any active recovery. Only fulfilled execution stop and settled recovery proceed to the original final admit=false sweep and original pendingCompletion rejection. Duplicate stop returns the same wrapper Promise and does not reinvoke execution.stop. Its original rejection propagates unchanged (active recovery catches only source sweep failures with the original fixed logger code); rejection never advances server shared Drive final stop.

The normal wake captures admit=!stopped at issuance. An active sweep issued **before** stop may finish its previously admitted claim; stop awaits that issuance before cancel/execution.stop, so it cannot issue after the original execution begins shutdown. All later microtask/timer/manual wake calls use admit=false and never call claim. Normal prune remains after successful admit=true sweep with original60000/history limits; stop recovery does not introduce maintenance/prune transactions. An initial queued microtask cannot admit after synchronous stop sets stopped. createMachineRunner has no start() API: construction creates timer1 and queueMicrotask. stop-before-initial-microtask and direct-wake active cases use the same timer; timer count1, interval2000, added timer0, no new deadline/loop.

Recovery sweep failures remain first-sticky as the original unknown error object, with original fixed log code and no property inspection. The interval may still run legitimate same-proof recovery, allowing the original callback to naturally settle. After original stop settles, any sticky recovery failure is rethrown and cannot produce a normal stop. If missing proof/irreversible recovery prevents operation.done, the original stop remains pending/held with its recovery timer; there is no finite timeout that fabricates callback completion. Outer runtime deadline/known owned-process force classification remains a separate later tool responsibility; no actual process closure is claimed here. Original stop rejection clears the recovery timer after original settlement and does not release unknown ownership. Original server caller-allSettled→shared final stop order, all unknown/proof/native gates and C0 void ACK/deferred/resource behavior remain outside this two-path delta.

## Prepared meaningful logical tests (execution0)

1. stop before initial microtask: all sweep calls admit=false, original logical stop once, repeated stop same Promise, final wake/timer creates no work.
2. manually-issued active admit=true sweep: stop does not invoke execution until that sweep completes; original logical stop publishes a pending flag only after immediate recover has run; one existing2000ms interval recover-only sweep resolves a separate logical completion gate; stop remains pending until then; subsequent sweeps admit=false and timer clears only after stop.
3. recover-only throws original logical error then a later sweep permits logical callback completion: stop rejects the same error and caches rejection instead of normal acceptance.
4. original logical execution.stop rejects: same error object reaches caller and duplicate stop has same Promise, timer cleared.
